nodes.label: ADR-001: Role Mapping Between DB and UI

nodes.label: ADR-004: Edge Function + n8n Cron Pattern
nodes.norm_label: adr-004: edge function + n8n cron pattern

nodes.label: Role Mapping Option A
nodes.rationale: Default mapping: add super_admin to the DB role enum and collapse admin/hr/cos/ceo into a single UI 'admin' role, aligning DB and UI roles while keeping the UI role surface small and preventing authorization drift.

nodes.label: Role Mapping Option B
nodes.rationale: Alternate mapping (hr/ceo -> admin, cos -> super_admin) kept available via NEXT_PUBLIC_ROLE_MAPPING_MODE=option-b so switching role semantics is a configuration change rather than a code change.

nodes.label: Trigger-Based Resource Analytics Counters
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER trigger functions increment view/bookmark/download counters synchronously to avoid application-level race conditions; a queue/cron batch approach was rejected as unnecessary infrastructure and eventual-consistency complexity at current traffic scale.

nodes.label: Supabase Storage for Resources
nodes.rationale: Supabase Storage integrates natively with RLS on storage.objects, avoiding a separate CDN authorization layer; signed URLs enforce access control at the data layer per Zero-Trust principles. External CDN (CloudFront/R2) was rejected as unnecessary infrastructure complexity at current scale.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Full-Text Search for Resources
nodes.rationale: A GIN index on tsvector handles stemming/ranking without external dependencies at the expected resource scale (hundreds to low thousands); Algolia/Elasticsearch were rejected due to added cost and data-sync complexity unjustified at current scale.

nodes.label: Linked-List Resource Versioning (previous_version_id)
nodes.rationale: Self-referential previous_version_id keeps versioning in a single table with minimal overhead since resources rarely exceed 2-3 versions; a separate resource_versions table was rejected as unjustified normalization/join complexity for the expected low version count.

nodes.label: Edge Function + n8n Cron Pattern
nodes.rationale: All automated workflows standardize on Supabase Edge Function (business logic, Deno) + n8n Schedule Trigger (cron) + thin Next.js API route shim (webhook-triggered only), because n8n gives visual workflow management, retries, execution history, and Gmail alerting without a Vercel Pro plan, while Edge Functions provide isolated service-role execution.

nodes.label: Vercel Cron to n8n Migration
nodes.rationale: Vercel Cron (and its per-job Next.js API shim + CRON_SECRET) was replaced by n8n workflows on flow.sngroup.cloud calling Edge Functions directly via HTTP POST, adding Gmail failure alerting on every workflow; API route shims were kept only for webhook/user-initiated functions.

nodes.label: Enum-to-Table Migration for resource_categories
nodes.rationale: Replaced the static resource_category enum with a resource_categories table (hierarchical parent_id, display_order, is_active, slugs, icons) because enum changes require risky ALTER TYPE migrations, cannot carry metadata or hierarchy, and block admin self-service; a JSONB column was rejected for lacking referential integrity, and a many-to-many tags table was rejected because categories are singular and hierarchical.

nodes.label: Knowledge Source Version Snapshot Trigger
nodes.rationale: A BEFORE UPDATE trigger (snapshot_knowledge_source_version) copies the old title/content into knowledge_source_versions before every edit, giving zero-config versioning, full rollback via restore_knowledge_source_version(), and an audit trail, without requiring every application edit path to manually version content; application-level versioning, diff-based storage, temporal tables, and audit-log-only approaches were all rejected.

nodes.label: Self-Feedback Iteration Loop
nodes.rationale: Requires a Plan -> Implement -> Self-Review -> Fix -> Validate -> Done loop before any task is declared complete, so that issues (any-types, missing tests, RLS gaps, sensitive-data leaks) are caught before merge rather than discovered later.
